newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian premier says "power ministers" to stay on.
newsitem.headline: Russian premier says "power ministers" to stay on.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Friday the interior and defence ministers and the head of the Federal Security Service would not be affected by a cabinet reshuffle now under way.

"There will be no personnel changes in any power structures now," he told the State Duma lower house of parliament. President Boris Yeltsin launched a dramatic cabinet reshuffle on Monday which is expected to be completed early next week.
The so-called "power ministers", who are responsible for maintaining national security, report directly to Yeltsin, as does the foreign minister too, bypassing the prime minister.
Some of them, including Defence Minister Igor Rodionov who has been publicly at odds with members of Yeltsin's entourage, had been rumoured to be facing the axe in the reshuffle.
Chernomyrdin told the Duma that further nominations would be made early next week to fill new posts established by the government shake-up but he added there would be no more sackings.

Yeltsin, worried by growing public discontent over a protracted economic downturn, has put pro-market liberals in broad control of economic policy. The president was in Helsinki on Friday for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
